canonical_statement: The PIANO study compared pregnancy and neonatal outcomes among IBD pregnancies exposed in utero to biologics, thiopurines, or combination therapy versus pregnancies unexposed to biologics or thiopurines, and also assessed placental transfer and childhood developmental milestones.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: We performed a prospective cohort study at selected US centers to assess pregnancy outcomes after in utero exposure to thiopurines, biologics, and combination therapy, and measured maternal–infant placental transfer of monoclonal antibodies and infant achievement of developmental milestones.

canonical_statement: PIANO was a prospective observational multicenter study enrolling pregnant women with IBD at 30 U.S. centers from January 2007 through March 2019.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The PIANO (Pregnancy in Inflammatory Bowel Disease and Neonatal Outcomes) study is a prospective observational study that enrolled pregnant women with IBD at 30 US centers between January 2007 and March 2019

canonical_statement: Eligible participants were pregnant women with inflammatory bowel disease and singleton pregnancies.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Only women with IBD and singleton pregnancies were eligible for inclusion.

population.label: Pregnant women with IBD and singleton pregnancies

canonical_statement: Of 1712 patients enrolled, 1490 completed pregnancies and 1431 resulted in live births; one-year measurements were available for 1010 offspring.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Of 1712 patients enrolled, 1490 completed pregnancies, with 1431 live births. One-year measurements were available in 1010 offspring.

canonical_statement: The 1490 completed pregnancies comprised 379 unexposed, 642 biologic-exposed, 242 thiopurine-exposed, and 227 combination-exposed pregnancies.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Exposure was to thiopurines (n = 242), biologics (n = 642), or both (n = 227) vs unexposed (n = 379).

canonical_statement: Medication exposure was defined as thiopurine or biologic use in the 3 months before the last menstrual period or at any time during pregnancy.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Exposure was defined as use of thiopurines or biologic in the 3 months before last menstrual period or any time during pregnancy.

concept.text: Thiopurines or biologics during the exposure window

exposures.details: 3 months before last menstrual period through pregnancy

canonical_statement: Participants were classified as unexposed, thiopurine exposed, biologic exposed, or combination exposed; the unexposed group could include mesalamine, corticosteroids, and antibiotics.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Women were assigned to 1 of 4 groups based on drug exposure: unexposed (includes mesalamine, corticosteroids, and antibiotics); thiopurine exposed; biologic exposed; and combination (both thiopurine and biologic) exposed.

canonical_statement: The primary outcomes were congenital malformations, spontaneous abortion, preterm birth before 37 weeks, low birth weight below 2500 g, and serious or nonserious infant infections.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The primary outcomes of the study were rates of congenital malformations, SAB, preterm birth, LBW, and infections (serious and nonserious) in the 3 exposure groups, relative to the unexposed group.

concept.text: Composite set of primary pregnancy and infant outcomes

outcome.definition: Congenital malformations, spontaneous abortion, preterm birth <37 weeks, low birth weight <2500 g, and infant infections

canonical_statement: A serious infant infection was defined as an infection requiring hospitalization; a nonserious infection was any reported infection not requiring hospitalization.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Infections were categorized into serious infections (requiring hospitalization) or nonserious infection (any reported infection without hospitalization).

outcome.definition: Serious = requiring hospitalization; nonserious = reported infection without hospitalization

canonical_statement: Crohn disease activity was measured with the Harvey-Bradshaw Index and ulcerative colitis activity with the Simple Clinical Colitis Activity Index; remission or mild activity was treated as inactive and moderate or severe activity as active in additional analyses.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Disease activity was measured using the Harvey-Bradshaw Index for CD and Simple Clinical Colitis Activity Index for UC. In additional analyses, remission or mild disease was considered inactive and moderate or severe disease was considered active.

canonical_statement: Adjusted logistic regression models for pregnancy complications controlled for maternal age, steroid use, and disease activity.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Logistic regression models controlling for maternal age, steroid use, and disease activity.

canonical_statement: Spontaneous-abortion risk analyses were restricted to women enrolled before 20 weeks and used Cox proportional hazards models including medication exposure, maternal age, disease activity, and prior spontaneous abortion.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: For analyses of SAB, we limited the cohort to those enrolled before 20 weeks’ gestation. We used Cox proportional hazard models to determine factors associated with SAB by 20 weeks, including medication exposures, maternal age, disease activity, and prior SAB.

canonical_statement: Developmental milestones were assessed with the Ages and Stages Questionnaire, 3rd edition, in communication, fine motor, gross motor, personal-social, and problem-solving domains at 12, 24, 36, and 48 months.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Developmental milestones were assessed through the nationally validated Ages and Stages Questionnaire, 3rd edition (ASQ3), at 12, 24, 36, and 48 months of age

canonical_statement: Maternal, cord, and infant biologic concentrations were measured at delivery in a subset; concentrations were analyzed continuously and in prespecified categories of low (0-3), therapeutic (3-10), high (10-20), and very high (>20).

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: For purposes of analysis we considered a trough concentration of 0–3 to be low, 3–10 therapeutic, 10–20 high, and >20 very high. Drug concentration at birth was analyzed as both a continuous variable as well as by category

canonical_statement: The study relied substantially on maternal self-report and lacked objective markers of IBD disease activity, creating potential outcome and disease-activity misclassification.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The limitations include the self-reported nature of the data and lack of objective markers of disease activity. It is possible that there is misclassification bias, as data are reported by mothers rather than ascertained from the medical record.

canonical_statement: Loss to follow-up could introduce selection bias; the supplement reports that 146 of 1712 enrolled women (8.5%) did not reach an end-of-pregnancy outcome while no longer pregnant, including 128 lost to follow-up and 18 who withdrew consent.

canonical_statement: The spontaneous-abortion rate is likely underestimated because many women enrolled after early pregnancy losses could already have occurred.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: We recognize that many women do not enroll into the cohort until later in pregnancy and that many SAB may occur prior to enrolling. Therefore, we expect the SAB rate detected to be lower than actual rate.
